terms.x: an iterator that wraps an iterator
terms.p: A method such as map or filter that returns a new iterator wrapping the old one and does no work at all until something asks it for an element.

terms.x: the thing that actually runs the chain
terms.p: A method such as collect, sum or count that calls next until the iterator is finished, which is the only point at which any of the work happens.
Building a description of a computation and doing none of it until a result is demanded, so work that is never needed is never performed.

terms.x: a trait method that comes pre-written
terms.p: A method a trait supplies a body for, so every implementor gets it free and only overrides it when it has a faster way.
Wrapping an iterator so that once it has returned None it keeps returning None, which the trait itself does not promise.
The trait a collection implements to say it can be built out of an iterator, which is what lets collect produce a Vec, a String, a HashMap or a Result.
